tasks.short: Stamp incoming mail with its receipt date and time.

steps.what: Collect incoming mail and position each item for receipt marking.
Apply receipt date and time with date-stamping equipment {OTHER}.
Check receipt marks and correct missing or illegible impressions.

tasks.design: Configure intake capture in the {WORKFLOW} to assign an item identifier and receipt timestamp, linked to a scan in the {DOCS}. The clerk presents physical items and reviews capture exceptions; retain physical stamping for items whose approved handling rules require it.
tasks.previous_blocker: The receipt mark travelled with the physical envelope. Digital intake may have been separate, making a second record more work than stamping.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing capture software can attach timestamps and identifiers without a model. Configuration and a small connector can join the intake event to the document record.
tasks.still_hard: Capture time may differ from delivery time. Clock errors, missed items and rules requiring physical marks need explicit handling; digital records also need GDPR access and retention controls.
tasks.human_edge: Notice damaged, misdelivered or sensitive items and preserve evidence when normal intake cannot establish receipt reliably.

ambition.what: Searchable receipt confirmation for internal recipients

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into repeated stamping and checking impressions. The clerk can investigate missing-mail queries from receipt records; formal receipt definitions remain with the records owner.

reach.task: Link incoming documents to retained records.
reach.learn: Document identifiers, retention classes and evidence-preserving corrections.

evidence.claim: PostNL offers business-mail scanning and conversion of forms into data.
Timestamp assignment and item identifiers can use deterministic configuration; physical handling remains.

assumptions: This describes an in-house mailroom handling modest daily batches.
The main path covers routine items eligible for digital receipt records.
An existing scanner can be used; purchasing or installing hardware is outside the estimates.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
Initial scanning effort must be measured because it can offset stamping savings.
unknowns: Which items require a physical receipt mark?
What event establishes receipt for legal or contractual deadlines?
Can existing capture software link item identifiers, timestamps and scans?
How much incoming mail already enters a digital intake process?
What access approvals and consultation under national rules are required?
research_questions: Does a trial preserve receipt evidence while reducing total handling time?
Can capture failures be detected through batch reconciliation before mail leaves intake?
new_work: Review failed captures, duplicate identifiers and incorrect timestamps.
Maintain receipt definitions and physical-stamping exceptions.
Check clock synchronisation, access permissions and retention settings.
Train clerks and complete applicable employee consultation under national rules.

tasks.short: Unload printed, folded, labelled or postmarked materials from mail-processing machines.

steps.what: Check mail-processing equipment {OTHER} has finished and is safe to unload.
Remove materials from mail-processing equipment {OTHER} and keep batches separate.
Inspect unloaded materials and separate damaged, mixed or incomplete output.
Mark the job ticket complete and record rejected output.

tasks.design: Replace the paper job ticket with a batch record in the {WORKFLOW}, using a scan or short confirmation to record completion and rejected output. Unloading, safe access and physical quality checks remain with the clerk; no model is needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Most effort is lifting and separating physical output. Software cannot remove that work, and a separate application can add more administration than it saves.
tasks.enabler_now: A small configured batch form can reuse an existing job identifier and remove handwritten completion details. This is a modest paperwork improvement, with no physical automation breakthrough.
tasks.still_hard: Mixed sizes, static, jams and damaged output require hands-on handling. Hardware changes need a separate equipment assessment and budget.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise unsafe conditions and defects that machine completion signals do not establish.
tasks.altitude: The week remains dominated by physical unloading and inspection. Completion paperwork shrinks slightly; decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Plan maintenance for recurring mailroom equipment faults.
reach.learn: Fault categories, safe isolation procedures and maintenance escalation criteria.

evidence.claim: Physical unloading and inspection generally remain manual without changes to equipment.
A configured batch form can reduce completion paperwork, but offers little saving on this predominantly physical task.

assumptions: The mailroom uses existing folding, franking or labelling equipment.
A paper job ticket records completion for batches that need traceability.
An existing {WORKFLOW} is available; a new platform would be disproportionate for this task alone.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Estimates exclude equipment modification and automated material handling.
unknowns: Are job tickets already digital?
Which batches require completion and reject records?
Can the existing {WORKFLOW} reuse current job identifiers?
How often do faults, heavy loads or mixed batches interrupt unloading?
What access and employee consultation under national rules apply to batch records?
research_questions: Does a digital completion action take less time than the current job-ticket entry?
Would physical changes to trays or batch sizes improve handling more than software?
new_work: Maintain batch identifiers and reject categories.
Resolve missing or duplicate completion records.
Train staff to distinguish machine completion from inspected batch acceptance.

tasks.short: Enter routing instructions to direct mail through computer-controlled equipment.

steps.what: Consult the routing directory in the {DOCS} for destinations and exceptions.
Present each item to mail-routing equipment {OTHER}.
Read the addressee and determine the destination using the routing scheme.

loop.input: Address-region image that barcode, OCR and exact directory matching could not resolve.
loop.output: Proposed recipient and location with supporting text regions, or unresolved.
loop.check: Require visible address evidence and a valid directory entry; the clerk approves model-derived routing instructions.
loop.stop: One extraction attempt per unresolved item; ambiguity, missing evidence or timeout sends it to manual routing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Barcodes, OCR and exact rules handle standard items. A bounded extraction pass can help with unusual address layouts; duplicate names still require a person.

steps.what: Key or speak the destination into mail-routing equipment {OTHER}.
Check diverted items and correct rejects or obvious routing errors.

tasks.design: Publish an approved routing directory from the {HCM} and {DOCS} to the {WORKFLOW}, then use barcodes, OCR and exact matching to prepare destination codes for mail-routing equipment {OTHER}. A bounded model extracts unresolved address text for clerk approval; a deterministic connector submits validated instructions and records rejects.
tasks.previous_blocker: Routing directories, address reading and machine entry were separate. Older equipment may expose only a console, while stale location records make unattended routing unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: Directory synchronisation, OCR and destination validation are established techniques. AI-assisted development can reduce connector work, while a bounded model may handle a limited residue of unusual labels.
tasks.still_hard: Unsupported machine interfaces can dominate cost. Duplicate names, confidential envelopes and staff moves need controlled exceptions; GDPR and EU AI Act obligations must be assessed for the actual use.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve ambiguous identities and recognise confidential or unusual deliveries before they reach the wrong recipient.

ambition.what: Pre-routing checks for staff moves and departures

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time entering destination codes and more time resolving ambiguous deliveries. They gain responsibility to correct provisional routing mappings, with employee-record changes still approved by the records owner.

reach.task: Coordinate mail-routing changes during office moves.
reach.learn: Directory ownership, location effective dates and testing of routing changes.

evidence.claim: PostNL offers physical-document digitisation and conversion of forms into data.
Paperbox organises insurance emails and attachments into case files; this supports classification feasibility, not physical sorter integration.
Exact directory matching and machine destination-code submission can be deterministic when interfaces exist.

assumptions: This task concerns internal destinations, not external dispatch decisions.
The company has computer-controlled routing equipment; smaller offices may route mail entirely by hand.
A supported machine interface and image capture are available; hardware replacement is outside the estimates.
Time shares, review effort and build ranges are planning estimates.
Model-derived routes require approval; exact deterministic matches can follow approved routing rules automatically.
unknowns: Does the routing equipment accept destination codes through a supported interface?
Are barcodes, address images or OCR already available?
Which directory is authoritative for staff locations and shared departments?
What proportion of items have ambiguous, handwritten or obsolete addresses?
What personal data may the connector and model process?
Which access approvals and consultation under national rules apply?
research_questions: How accurately do barcode, OCR and exact matching route a representative labelled sample?
Does a bounded extraction pass save review time on the unresolved residue?
Can the connector reconcile every item with a destination or an explicit reject?
Does routing quality remain acceptable during directory changes and equipment outages?
new_work: Review model-derived destinations and unresolved identities.
Maintain aliases, shared destinations and effective dates.
Reconcile rejected items and failed machine submissions.
Sample routing accuracy and maintain a manual fallback.
Maintain access controls, model checks and applicable consultation records.

tasks.short: Wrap or tie outgoing packages and bundles securely.

steps.what: Assess outgoing items and choose suitable wrapping materials.
Wrap items by hand or secure bundles with tying equipment {OTHER}.
Check wrapping strength, closures and item protection before releasing packages for dispatch.

tasks.design: Publish a short packing guide in the {DOCS}, using fixed choices for common item sizes and fragility classes, and place matching supplies at the workstation. The clerk chooses, wraps and checks each package; no model or new application is needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: The main work requires dexterity and judgement about physical objects. Software cannot wrap mixed packages, and dedicated machinery needs sufficient repeat volume.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing instructions and standard materials can be organised into a reusable guide cheaply. There is no new technical breakthrough for the physical work.
tasks.still_hard: Irregular, fragile or confidential contents require individual handling. Packing quality depends on materials, technique and physical inspection.
tasks.human_edge: Feel weak closures, judge awkward shapes and protect contents whose condition cannot be captured reliably in a simple form.
tasks.altitude: Common packaging choices become slightly quicker. The week remains physical and decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Investigate damage linked to packaging choices.
reach.learn: Carrier packing requirements, damage categories and how to revise packing instructions.

evidence.claim: A fixed packing guide can reduce repeated material-selection effort for standard items.
Wrapping and checking mixed physical packages remain manual without equipment changes.

assumptions: Outgoing items vary enough that a new automated packing line is outside scope.
Common items can use a small set of approved packaging choices.
The existing {DOCS} can hold the guide without additional licence cost.
Run cost means incremental software cost; packing supplies and labour continue.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Which sizes, weights and fragility classes account for most packages?
Are packing instructions already available at the workstation?
Which carrier or contents restrictions apply?
What damage and repacking records exist?
Does any workstation change require consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Does the guide reduce selection time without increasing damage or material use?
Would changes to supply placement save more time than a digital guide?
new_work: Keep packing choices aligned with available supplies and carrier requirements.
Review damage feedback and revise instructions.
Train staff on unusual items and escalation criteria.

role.altitude: The role remains grounded in physical handling, safe equipment use and delivery accuracy. Digital intake and routing can shift some time toward tracing missing items and resolving exceptions; they do not automatically grant authority over employee records, retention policy or equipment safety.
reach: File clerk: connect receipt records to document retention and retrieval.
Administrative services manager: coordinate routing changes during office moves.
Facilities manager: turn recurring equipment faults into maintenance requests.
Shipping clerk: use damage feedback to improve packing instructions.
skills_to_grow: Receipt evidence, document retention and GDPR access controls
Checking extracted text against visible evidence
Recognising applicable EU AI Act duties and consultation requirements under national rules
Safe equipment handling and packaging quality
role.ambitious_version: Offer a shared intake and routing service that provides receipt confirmation and resolves ambiguous deliveries across office locations, while clerks retain control of physical handling and sensitive exceptions.

job.title: Mail Clerks and Mail Machine Operators, Except Postal Service
